reproduction_target: Reproduce, from the Illumina MiniSeq paired-end RNA-seq reads of two archived Indian EV-A71 isolates (R13223-IND-02, genogroup D; V11-2209-01, genogroup G) plus a circulating C1 sub-genogroup isolate, the complete-genome consensus sequences (fastp 0.23.4 read trimming/QC, Trinity 2.15.2 de novo transcriptome assembly with default parameters), the genogroup assignment and Neighbor-Joining phylogeny of the assembled genomes against representative EV-A71 full-length genomes downloaded from NCBI GenBank (MAFFT v7.490 multiple sequence alignment, MEGA6 NJ tree with Maximum Composite Likelihood distances, pairwise deletion, 1000 bootstrap replicates), the reported whole-genome and per-protein nucleotide/amino-acid divergence percentages, and the gene-wise synonymous/non-synonymous mutation profiles of genogroups D and G against four reference strains (U22521 genogroup A, DQ341365 B4, LC626884 C4, CSF31-IND-01 C1) reported in Table 1. Retrieval of the archived isolates from the ICMR-NIV Mumbai repository, RD-cell propagation, partial VP1 serotyping, RNA extraction, rRNA depletion, library preparation and Illumina sequencing are out of scope (W).
granularity_note: Methods is a single ~450-word 'Methodology' section with no workflow file, no code repository and no command lines. Steps were derived one per named tool or named analysis invocation, giving 7 computational steps (C1-C7) and 6 wet-lab steps (W1-W6). C6 (divergence estimation) and C7 (mutation profiling) are separated because they are reported as distinct result families (percent identity/divergence tables vs. the Table-1 gene-wise mutation counts) even though neither names a tool; if a shared canonical step list merges them, |S| becomes 6 and both verdicts stay NI, so no ratio changes materially. Two internal inconsistencies were recorded rather than resolved: (a) library preparation is described twice with two different kits in consecutive sentences - verbatim 'the total RNA was used for library preparation by using truesq LT library preparation kit. RNA libraries were prepared using TruSeq Stranded mRNA Library Prep Kit'; (b) the Methods say complete-genome sequencing was also performed on the circulating C1 sub-genogroup isolate (CSF31-IND-01, used as a Table-1 comparator), but no accession is given for it anywhere in the paper, unlike the two indigenous isolates.

steps.label: Raw paired-end read processing with fastp version 0.23.4 - adapter trimming, quality filtering, per-read quality correction and QC report generation
De novo transcriptome assembly of the trimmed reads with Trinity version 2.15.2 'with default parameters', yielding the complete EV-A71 genomes
Retrieval of the phylogeny reference panel - 'representative full length genomes of various genogroups were downloaded from the NCBI GenBank database' (no accession list, no download date, no query)
Multiple sequence alignment of the nucleotide sequences with the MAFFT software package, MAFFT v7.490 (no alignment strategy, iteration or scoring options stated)

Phylogenetic reconstruction in MEGA6 - Neighbor-Joining method, Maximum Composite Likelihood evolutionary distances (base substitutions per site), pairwise deletion of gaps/missing data, 1000 bootstrap replicates (Fig. 1)

Whole-genome and per-protein nucleotide divergence / amino-acid identity estimation across genogroups (reported as 12.57%-20.33% nucleotide divergence, >95% amino-acid identity, up to ~9.5% protein-level divergence) - no tool, method or distance model named for this computation

Gene-wise synonymous / non-synonymous mutation profiling of genogroups D and G against four reference strains (U22521, DQ341365, LC626884, CSF31-IND-01), annotated relative to the genotype-A reference - verbatim 'The amino acid mutations were analysed in the aligned file. Common and unique mutations for the genogroups of interest were obtained by comparative analysis' (Table 1)

Retrieval of the VP1-characterised D and G genogroup isolates (originally from AFP faecal samples collected in 2001 and 2011 under the WHO AFP surveillance network) and of the circulating C1 isolate from the ICMR-NIV Mumbai repository, propagated in RD cells
NPEV serotype identification by partial VP1 sequencing, 'as previously described' (ref. 18) - no protocol restated
RNA extraction using the KingFisher Flex RNA extractor (Thermo Fisher Scientific)
Ribosomal RNA depletion by probe hybridisation and thermostable RNase H digestion, followed by DNase I removal of genomic DNA and residual probe

Stranded RNA library preparation and QC - the paper names two different kits in consecutive sentences ('truesq LT library preparation kit' and 'TruSeq Stranded mRNA Library Prep Kit'), followed by Qubit dsDNA high-sensitivity quantification and normalisation
Next-generation sequencing of the normalised libraries on the Illumina MiniSeq platform (no read length, run configuration or target depth stated)

headline.static_readiness: 0/7 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification). Unexecuted; under-claims by construction - Tier-1 cannot credit an undeclared-but-present dependency. There is no declared environment of any kind here: no lockfile, no container, no conda/mamba environment file, no requirements file and no code repository, so nothing is even claimed that a stage-2 pass could verify. has_validated_env_capture = false, n_exact_capture_unexecuted = 0, n_fetch_required = 0.
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: 1/7 (14%) readiness upper bound at stage 1: (n_R + n_RI) / |S| = (0 + 1) / 7. The single RI step is C5 (MEGA6 Neighbor-Joining phylogeny), which is the only step where all four axes reach 1 - the method, distance model, gap handling and bootstrap replicate count are all stated, the two study genomes are in GenBank (PX260179, PX260180, both resolve, 7403 nt and 7402 nt, updated 2026-02-23), and a version string exists even though it is major-only ('MEGA6'). It is capped at RI regardless by the stochastic-no-seed ceiling: 1000 bootstrap replicates with no seed and no seed-consumption evidence, so only distributional agreement of support values could be claimed (subflag distributional-only). The two binding constraints elsewhere are (a) the raw sequencing data axis - the Illumina MiniSeq paired-end reads are never deposited and no SRA/ENA/BioProject accession appears anywhere, so C1 and C2 (fastp, Trinity) sit at data = 0 and the assembly half of the paper cannot be re-run at all; and (b) the code axis - no repository, script, command line or notebook is cited anywhere in the paper, so C3, C6 and C7 sit at code = 0 with no named tool at all for the divergence and mutation-profiling analyses that produce Table 1 and most of the Results. Version reporting is the one relative strength: fastp 0.23.4, Trinity 2.15.2 and MAFFT v7.490 carry exact prose pins, which is why capture_claim is exact_pins_partial rather than floating - but exact prose pins without environment closure cap the version axis at 1 by construction (rubric Delta-2), so a stage-2 code check would yield zero R-star gain here even if code appeared.
headline.coverage: computational coverage |S| / (|S| + |W|) = 7 / 13 = 54%; 6 wet-lab steps (repository isolate retrieval and RD-cell propagation, partial VP1 serotyping, KingFisher RNA extraction, rRNA depletion, library preparation and QC, Illumina MiniSeq sequencing) scored OOS. This is a genome-characterisation paper whose wet-lab half is roughly as large as its computational half; the computational half is short (two assembly steps plus five alignment/phylogeny/comparison steps), so |S| = 7 is close to the rubric's |S| >= 4 floor and per-paper ratios should be read with that small denominator in mind.

gaps.where: Entire Methodology section - computational steps C1-C7
gaps.missing: No code repository, script, notebook, command line, container or workflow file is cited anywhere in the paper. There is no Code Availability statement. The Data Availability statement reads verbatim: 'The authors declare that the data supporting the findings of this study is available in the article and supplementary material.' The only supplementary item is 'Supplementary Table.docx'. Three of the seven computational steps (C3 reference retrieval, C6 divergence estimation, C7 mutation profiling) name no tool at all, and C7 produces Table 1 and the substantive Results. Verbatim for C7: 'The amino acid mutations were analysed in the aligned file. Common and unique mutations for the genogroups of interest were obtained by comparative analysis.'
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the analysis scripts (or, at minimum, the exact fastp / Trinity / MAFFT command lines and the MEGA6 session or the script used to tabulate the divergence percentages and the Table-1 mutation counts) in a public repository with an archival DOI, and add a Code Availability statement pointing at it.

gaps.where: Data Availability statement; computational steps C1 and C2 (fastp, Trinity)
gaps.missing: The Illumina MiniSeq raw paired-end reads for the two indigenous isolates and for the C1 comparator are not deposited: no SRA, ENA, BioProject or BioSample accession appears anywhere in the paper, and the availability statement points only to 'the article and supplementary material'. Only the two finished consensus genomes were deposited (GenBank PX260179, PX260180). Consequently the input to the read-processing and assembly steps is unavailable, sample-to-raw-data correspondence is absent, and the two steps that actually produce the paper's central claim - the first complete genomes of genogroups D and G from India - are unreproducible from any starting point. There is additionally no accession at all for the third sequenced isolate, the C1 sub-genogroup strain CSF31-IND-01, despite the Methods stating it underwent complete genome sequencing and despite its use as a Table-1 comparator.
gaps.how_to_close: Submit the raw reads to SRA/ENA under a BioProject with per-isolate BioSamples, cite the run accessions in the availability statement, and deposit the CSF31-IND-01 genome in GenBank with its accession cited in the text.

gaps.where: C3 (NCBI GenBank reference retrieval), feeding C4 (MAFFT), C5 (MEGA6) and C7 (mutation profiling)
gaps.missing: The phylogeny reference panel is described only as 'representative full length genomes of various genogroups were downloaded from the NCBI GenBank database'. No accession list, no query string, no download date, no GenBank release, and no supplementary sequence table. Some accessions appear incidentally in the Results and figure legend (AY179600, KF906423, KF906420, KF906417.1, JN204010, JN204017, JN204025, U22521, DQ341365, LC626884) but these are cited as clade neighbours or comparators, not as the alignment input set, and the set is manifestly incomplete relative to a tree resolving genogroups A-G and sub-genogroups B0-B5 / C1-C5. GenBank is a rolling resource, so this is an unpinned external reference-database dependency. Note that env_capture_class is deliberately left 'n/a' rather than classified B or C: A/B/C classification requires reading executable workflow code, which does not exist for this paper.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the full accession list (with GenBank versions, e.g. AY179600.1) of every sequence in the alignment as a supplementary table, and state the retrieval date; better still, deposit the alignment FASTA itself.

gaps.where: C5 (MEGA6); C6 and C7 (no tool named) - dictionary subtype 2a (版記載なし), recorded as integer 2 because the schema requires gaps[].type to be an integer
gaps.missing: MEGA is cited only as 'MEGA6 software' - a major version with no minor or build (MEGA6 shipped as 6.0 through 6.06 with differing behaviour), so the version axis cannot exceed 1 and the subtier is 'floating'. C6 (divergence and identity percentages) and C7 (synonymous/non-synonymous mutation calling and annotation against the genotype-A reference U22521) name no software whatsoever, so no version can be recorded for the steps that generate Table 1 and most of the Results narrative.
gaps.how_to_close: Report the exact MEGA build (e.g. MEGA 6.06) and name the tool used for the divergence and mutation comparisons with its version - or state explicitly that they were done manually in the MEGA alignment explorer.

gaps.missing: Bootstrap resampling with 1000 replicates is reported, but no random seed is given and MEGA6 does not record one in the published output. The reported support values (100% for the genogroup D clade, 99% for genogroup G, >90% for most clusters) are therefore reproducible only in distribution, not exactly. This caps C5 at RI (subflag distributional-only) independently of its axis scores.
gaps.how_to_close: State the bootstrap seed, or replace the MEGA6 GUI run with a scripted phylogeny (e.g. IQ-TREE / RAxML with -seed recorded) and deposit the run log.

gaps.where: C7 (Table 1 mutation profiling) - reference strain CSF31-IND-01
gaps.missing: One of the four Table-1 comparator strains, the Indian C1 sub-genogroup strain CSF31-IND-01, is identified only by an in-house strain name. The other three comparators carry public accessions (U22521, DQ341365, LC626884). The CSF31-IND-01 sequence is effectively an unreleased in-house reference, so the D-vs-C1 and G-vs-C1 mutation counts (78 and 89 non-synonymous substitutions respectively) - reported and interpreted at length in Results and Discussion - cannot be recomputed by a third party.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the CSF31-IND-01 complete genome in GenBank and cite its accession wherever the strain is used as a comparator.

gaps.missing: Six of thirteen steps are wet-lab (repository isolate retrieval and RD-cell propagation, partial VP1 serotyping deferred to reference 18, KingFisher Flex RNA extraction, RNase H rRNA depletion plus DNase I treatment, stranded library preparation with Qubit QC, Illumina MiniSeq sequencing). These are scored OOS and excluded from |S|, reducing computational coverage to 54%. Recorded here for completeness rather than as a defect of the computational assessment; the library-preparation step does however carry an unresolved internal inconsistency (two different kits named in consecutive sentences) and the sequencing step states no read length, run configuration or target depth.
gaps.how_to_close: Not applicable to computational reproducibility; for wet-lab transparency, resolve the library-kit inconsistency and report the sequencing run configuration and achieved depth per isolate.
